front: General structure of an amino acid?
back: Central C with an amine group (–NH₂), carboxyl group (–COOH), H and a variable R group.
The sequence of amino acids in a polypeptide, held by peptide bonds.
Hydrogen bonds between C=O and N–H of the backbone (α-helix, β-pleated sheet).
Hydrophobic interactions, hydrogen bonds, ionic bonds, disulfide bonds (all between R groups).
Two or more polypeptide chains (sometimes with a prosthetic group) forming one functional protein.
Loss of a protein's 3D shape when hydrogen, ionic (and other) bonds break; primary structure unchanged; function lost.
Globular: compact, soluble, physiological (enzymes). Fibrous: long, insoluble, structural (collagen).

front: Which amino acid forms disulfide bonds?
back: Cysteine (sulfur-containing R group); S–S bonds are covalent.
